initiatives.name: SMT Board Governance Restructuring
initiatives.summary: Heather Manners joined the Board as a Non-Executive Director effective 1 January 2026 and was appointed to chair the newly established Marketing Working Group.

evidence.title: New Director Heather Manners Appointed
evidence.summary: Heather Manners joined the Board as a Non-Executive Director effective 1 January 2026 and was appointed to chair the newly established Marketing Working Group.
evidence.quote: Following the appointment of Ms Heather Manners on 1 January 2026, the Board comprises seven Directors, all of whom are non-executive.

evidence.title: Professor Maxwell Board Retirement
evidence.summary: Professor Patrick Maxwell will retire from the Board following the conclusion of the Annual General Meeting on 2 July 2026, with Sharon Flood becoming Senior Independent Director in his place.
evidence.quote: As previously announced, Professor Maxwell will retire from the Board following the conclusion of the Annual General Meeting on 2 July 2026... Ms Flood will become the Senior Independent Director following Professor Maxwell's retirement.

evidence.title: New Remuneration Committee Established
evidence.summary: The Board established a new Remuneration Committee, chaired by Sharon Flood, with a broader remit than typical including Board effectiveness and development alongside Directors' fees responsibilities.
evidence.quote: During the year, the Board established a Remuneration Committee, chaired by Sharon Flood, with all other Directors serving as members. The Committee is expected to have a broader remit than is typical, encompassing certain aspects of Board effectiveness and development alongside its responsibilities in relation to Directors' fees.

evidence.title: New Marketing Working Group Established
evidence.summary: The Board established a Marketing Working Group chaired by Heather Manners to support oversight of the Company's marketing and shareholder engagement activities.
evidence.quote: The Board also established a Marketing Working Group, chaired by Heather Manners, to support oversight of the Company's marketing and shareholder engagement activities.

initiatives.name: SpaceX Portfolio Expansion and Public Listing
initiatives.summary: SpaceX acquired xAI, combining its aerospace and satellite connectivity business with frontier AI capabilities. The deal valued the combined entity at $1.25 trillion, positioning SpaceX at the intersection of launch, energy, and AI infrastructure.

evidence.title: SpaceX IPO Filing for Public Listing
evidence.summary: SpaceX filed documentation with regulators to go public, targeting a mid-June listing, which represents a major strategic transition for one of the Trust's largest private holdings. The Trust will be subject to a lock-up period as an existing holder.
evidence.quote: SpaceX is a private company, but in April 2026 it filed the documentation with regulators to go public, targeting a mid-June listing on the stock market.

evidence.title: SpaceX Acquisition of xAI
evidence.summary: SpaceX acquired xAI, combining its aerospace and satellite connectivity business with frontier AI capabilities. The deal valued the combined entity at $1.25 trillion, positioning SpaceX at the intersection of launch, energy, and AI infrastructure.
evidence.quote: In February 2026, its acquisition of xAI valued the combined entity at $1.25 trillion, uniting rockets and frontier AI under one roof.

evidence.title: SpaceX Acquisition of EchoStar Wireless Spectrum
evidence.summary: SpaceX acquired EchoStar's wireless spectrum to accelerate direct-to-phone satellite connectivity, eliminating the need for dedicated user terminals by allowing standard smartphones to connect directly to Starlink satellites.
evidence.quote: The acquisition of EchoStar's wireless spectrum accelerated the push into direct-to-phone connectivity, a development that eliminates the need for dedicated user terminals by allowing standard smartphones to connect directly to Starlink satellites.

initiatives.name: SMT Share Buyback Programme
initiatives.summary: The Company executed a large-scale share buyback programme to manage the discount to NAV, repurchasing 122.9 million shares during the year at a cost of £1.31 billion, totaling £3.02 billion over two years representing ~22% of issued share capital.

evidence.title: Share Buyback Programme
evidence.summary: The Company executed a large-scale share buyback programme to manage the discount to NAV, repurchasing 122.9 million shares during the year at a cost of £1.31 billion, totaling £3.02 billion over two years representing ~22% of issued share capital.
evidence.quote: During the year to 31 March 2026, the Company bought back 122.9 million shares at a total cost of £1.31 billion. Over the two-year period to 31 March 2026, the Company has bought back 307.7 million shares at a total cost of £3.02 billion, representing approximately 22% of the issued share capital as at 31 March 2024.

evidence.quote: Stripe completed its acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure platform Bridge in early 2025 for $1.1 billion.

initiatives.name: SMT Debt Facility Refinancing
initiatives.summary: The Company refinanced multiple expiring loan facilities during and after the year, replacing a US$300 million Scotiabank loan and US$75 million ICBC facility with new facilities from ICBC, Bank of New York Mellon, and BBVA, plus a post-year-end RBSI refinancing.
initiatives.investmentSummary: US$120 million (ICBC); US$75 million (BNY Mellon); US$150 million (BBVA); US$205 million (RBSI, post year-end)

evidence.title: Debt Facility Refinancing Programme
evidence.summary: The Company refinanced multiple expiring loan facilities during and after the year, replacing a US$300 million Scotiabank loan and US$75 million ICBC facility with new facilities from ICBC, Bank of New York Mellon, and BBVA, plus a post-year-end RBSI refinancing.
evidence.quote: During the year, the undrawn US$75 million revolving credit facility with Industrial and Commercial Bank of China ("ICBC") was refinanced with a new US$120 million revolving credit facility. The US$300 million Scotiabank three-year fixed-rate loan expired and was refinanced through drawdowns of US$120 million from the new ICBC facility, US$30 million from a new US$75 million revolving credit facility with The Bank of New York Mellon, and US$150 million from a new US$150 million revolving credit facility with Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria S.A.

evidence.quote: We exited Wayfair entirely, concluding that the headwinds facing US consumer discretionary spending had shifted the risk-reward beyond what we were willing to hold.

initiatives.name: ByteDance TikTok US Operations Resolution
initiatives.summary: ByteDance reached an agreement transferring majority control of TikTok's US operations to a US-led joint venture, resolving years of political and regulatory uncertainty while retaining a 19.9% stake and algorithm IP.

evidence.title: ByteDance TikTok US Operations Resolution
evidence.summary: ByteDance reached an agreement transferring majority control of TikTok's US operations to a US-led joint venture, resolving years of political and regulatory uncertainty while retaining a 19.9% stake and algorithm IP.
evidence.quote: In December 2025, ByteDance reached an agreement on TikTok's US operations, resolving years of political and regulatory uncertainty. Majority control transfers to a US-led joint venture, which assumes operational control of the recommendation algorithm for American users, while ByteDance retains a 19.9% stake and the underlying algorithm intellectual property.

initiatives.name: SMT Investment Policy Amendment for Private Companies
initiatives.summary: Shareholders approved an amendment to the Company's Investment Policy providing flexibility to invest up to £250 million additional capital in private companies when the existing 30% limit is exceeded, driven by market movements, revaluations, and the buyback programme.

evidence.title: Amended Investment Policy for Private Company Exposure
evidence.summary: Shareholders approved an amendment to the Company's Investment Policy providing flexibility to invest up to £250 million additional capital in private companies when the existing 30% limit is exceeded, driven by market movements, revaluations, and the buyback programme.
evidence.quote: The revised Investment Policy allows the Board, subject to shareholder approval and defined limits, to permit up to £250 million of additional investment in private companies when the existing limit has been exceeded.
